summary: The lecture introduces a full-fledged UPSC Environment & Ecology course covering 12 topics, emphasizing static concepts, current affairs integration, and previous year question analysis. It defines environment, ecology, ecosystem components, food chains, biogeochemical cycles, ecosystem services, and homeostasis. The faculty outlines study strategy using NCERTs, official websites, and practical examples like lemon grass repelling mosquitoes.
points: Course covers 12 topics (11 core + 1 miscellaneous) for Environment & Ecology.
UPSC Prelims: 2 papers (GS & CSAT), 200 marks each, 1/3 negative marking; Forest & Civil Services combined.
Environment = complex network of physical, biological, and social systems (biotic + abiotic).
Ecology term coined by German biologist Ernst Haeckel; studies organism-surroundings interaction & resource utilization.
Ecosystem = geographical area where plants, animals, species, weather, topography interact forming a living bubble.
Structural components: Abiotic (sun, soil, water) & Biotic (producers, consumers, decomposers).
Food chain: energy transfer from green plants through eating/being eaten; types: Grazing & Detritus.
Biogeochemical cycles: Gaseous (Carbon, Nitrogen - reservoir atmosphere) & Sedimentary (Phosphorus - reservoir lithosphere).
Ecosystem services: Provisioning (food, water), Regulating (climate, disease), Supporting (nutrient cycling), Cultural (recreation).
Homeostasis = ecosystem's ability to maintain stability despite disturbances; examples: hibernation, aestivation, brumation.
